note: Queries that do not resolve AS THE ROLE THEIR MODULE CONNECTS AS. See role_contract.mjs. Entries may only be REMOVED — never edited to hide a regression, and never added without a reason. A baselined site that starts passing fails the build, so this list can only shrink. 16 at R13-roleci; 15 after RF6-claim; 3 after R10-role-routing.
source: HP-RECON-004 — the request path has no role

entries.why: obs.ai_call INSERT is granted to redflag_role and to nothing else, but the request path logs COMPOSE and CATEGORY_CLASSIFY calls too, so moving anthropic.ts onto the red-flag pool would be the wrong shape. Needs obs.record_ai_call(...). ALSO BLOCKED ON A DECISION: ai_call.audit_id FKs to obs.response_audit(id), and every AI call is logged BEFORE the audit row exists (HP-RECON-006 §2). Decided 8 Sep: log NULL and backfill after the audit row lands.
entries.item: HP-RECON-006 §2 — the obs write functions, with the ordering fix

entries.why: obs.fabrication_block has no INSERT grant to any application role and RLS is on with one metrics-only SELECT policy. Needs obs.record_fabrication_block(...) — a DEFINER function, per the idiom obs.record_metric_sample already sets, rather than a direct grant.

The side-effect worker runs on the app's own DATABASE_URL, so it is hp_app, and it reads safety.clinician_alert — which hp_app cannot reach at all. It is also the consumer half of side_effect_job, the stub-invented queue R10b replaces with obs.review_queue_item. R10b is PARKED by decision: review_queue_item.clinical_domain is NOT NULL and nothing in the request path produces a clinical domain, so the reroute needs response-domain classification — which decides who is competent to review what, and is the clinical lead's call.
